agree.reason: The nurse's firsthand visit counts, the neighbouring district's results and the concrete fixes for each concern make a persuasive case, though a resisting board member may still see the athletics and drop-off answers as deferred rather than solved.

honest.reason: The piece declines the brief's unsupported graduation-rate claim and keeps the figures accurate, with only small additions beyond the facts: the general claim about teen sleep cycles and the assumption that the neighbouring district shares 'the same winter sunset.'

works_the_facts.reason: It works the raw numbers into useful forms (72 percent, mid-morning visits at 'less than half,' 84 percent as 'one in six' not finishing, and the neighbours having no four-year cohort yet), but it does not set the $180,000 against anything to make that cost concrete.

right_comparison.reason: Keeping 7:25 is presented as having its own ongoing costs in visits, lost class time and students falling behind, which fits the facts, though the brief has no trend data to show whether things are getting worse.

qualification.reason: The pledge to publish first-period attendance, tardies and nurse visits after one year, and to revisit if they don't improve, can be checked, but it sets no target number and no exact report date.

objections.reason: All three objections (bus cost, athletics, 8 a.m. drop-offs) are acknowledged and answered, but the athletics answer leans on asking the neighbours and the early-supervision idea adds an uncosted expense.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured op-ed timed to the April 14 vote and sits at about the 650-word limit, perhaps slightly over.
